newsitem.title: DUBAI: Egyptian pilgrims stranded at Saudi port.
newsitem.headline: Egyptian pilgrims stranded at Saudi port.

text.p: Over 1,000 Egyptian Moslem pilgrims seeking to return home have been stranded at Jeddah Islamic Port in Saudi Arabia for the last ten days, witnesses said on Sunday.
"They have been sleeping on sidewalks and streets around the port," one told Reuters. "The authorities have given them food and blankets."
Many of the Egyptians, who performed the minor Umra pilgrimage at Mecca, were elderly, the witnesses said.
Egyptian diplomats in Jeddah blamed the crisis on shipping companies in Egypt, saying they had issued tickets to the pilgrims without guaranteeing their return.
The Egyptian ambassador to Saudi Arabia, Mohammad Kamel Amr, told Reuters: "The crisis will be solved within 48 hours."
He said some of the shipping companies that had transported the pilgrims to Saudi Arabia had agreed to transfer the pilgrims to vessels from other firms leaving the Red Sea port.
Saudi police last week intervened to calm hundreds of enraged Egyptian Moslem pilgrims and regular travellers who got stranded at Jeddah airport because of seat shortages on Egypt Air.
Over 30,000 Egyptian pilgrims performed the Umra this year, a pilgrimage which can take place at any time of the year, diplomats said.
